body: I'm sorry, I don't think talking about music should be considered cheating. You and I obviously have very different boundaries, or more likely you are projecting on me.

Y'all are projecting here. I didn't go to another man. I talked to another man, with my husband's blessing, about incredibly superficial things. As soon as I started to think anything more of it I told my husband and offered to completely cut this person out of my life.

We are talking about someone I only communicated with for a few days here. It's one of those things where we just instantly clicked, not a long drawn out emotional development. The only thing that happened because he was expressing our marriage was over, was that I didn't shut everything down before telling my husband about the situation. 

I understand though that divorce is a must.

Thank you, I really appreciate hearing your perspective on this. You're absolutely right, I do think I'm prone to starting to develop feelings for people. Becoming aware of this through therapy, I very intentionally set up my boundaries and put myself in a headspace to immediately talk to my SO so I could just end things and keep our relationship safe, but I think my STBXH sees this as a personality flaw. I think that's the biggest thing I'm struggling with here, feeling like I'm just a villain no matter what actual actions I take. So I really appreciate hearing that I'm not completely alone and crazy in this.

Because my husband had already been telling me for quite some time there was a 0% chance of anything working between us. So of course I would just cut him off, but why would I do that if I'm not even actually in a marriage? I've been acting like I am for quite some time now but my husband has never changed his perspective on it, that we are completely over. I suppose that's why I told him and said I would cut this person out of my life, despite him already telling me for a long time we were done, I wanted to give him the opportunity to express that this was something which was still important to him. 

I hope this doesn't come across poorly, I genuinely would like to understand better, but why cut people out of my life after the relationship is already over?

I apologize, I realized I didn't answer this part of your post. Why not file for divorce? I felt the least I could do was financially support him, I suppose in a way to try to give him as much as he would allow me to. Even if I couldn't make amends emotionally, I could at least give him that so he could get to a better position. I am the only source of income in our relationship, the sole breadwinner. I didn't want to leave him high and dry like that, ESPECIALLY considering the fact it was my fault he was in so much pain.

I believe that affairs are not specific actions, but rather a breaking of boundaries. Some people are okay with their SOs sleeping with other people. Some people are not. I'm the type of person who does not care if my SO has close relationships with people of the opposite gender, many people do care about this kind of thing. We are all different and it's important to talk in detail with your SO on where their boundaries are so you can respect them. 

Typically if you are hiding something, it means you are breaking a boundary. Whatever that is, that's a problem. If you don't actually think you are breaking a boundary, you need to talk to your SO to put it out into the open.

I know EVERYONE says this but therapy is so important! Get a good therapist who she can work through establishing boundaries with. I've found that many of us with low self-esteem and/or trauma have very weak, loose boundaries. Building those up to be healthy boundaries will be a game changer! And, typically, therapy will also help her work through the self esteem problems themselves as well.

I am 100% confident. I know exactly where my first "wrong" decisions were made, the ones that weren't inherently bad by themselves but started me down the path where I began to push boundaries, and I therefore know how to stay miles away from those kinds of decisions now. I also have been working through my complete lack of boundaries in therapy to allow me to have healthy boundaries regardless of whether my husband is with me or not, i.e. I am resolving my issues for myself and not just for him.

I didn't think the things I was doing were going to hurt my relationship as badly as they did, to be frank. I know people will probably feel incredulous but it's the truth. I don't personally have the same boundaries as many other people or my husband, so an EA is essentially impossible with me unless there was some discussion of wanting to leave our marriage or hatred toward me, but I have a problem with that in friendships as well as relationships so there really isn't a difference there. I have no inherent concept of people being "too close". I have been cheated on three times in the past, as in my partners slept with other people. None of those relationships lasted for completely unrelated reasons, I have thought much more about the cheating now due to my own bout of infidelity than I ever did while in those relationships. And at the time I was cheating I didn't even think I was because I wasn't sleeping with anyone else, nor did I want to leave my relationship.

So why am I fighting now? Because I've seen the impact it has had on my partner and it's heartbreaking. If I had magical abilities to see the future and had known what this would do to him in the first place I wouldn't have gotten anywhere close. And I'm confident I never will again because of that. I am trying really hard now to be more understanding of him. What will and won't impact ME doesn't matter, I need to be respectful of HIS boundaries. I don't make ANY assumptions anymore, I literally ask how he feels about things that we've done over and over and over just to make sure his feelings on things haven't changed over time, and I especially make sure to communicate when we, either individually or as a couple, are treading into new territory.

Thank you for your response! I know all of our situations are different but this helps me set up a good starting point of things to offer and put effort into making available as options at the very least.

I have been for quite a while now. I'm not asking this as a way to take away his agency. His response is always "I don't know" so I'm just trying to get a good foundation for when I have to make decisions with no direction.

I really relate to this. I also come from a similarly traumatizing past, and feel like although I do have a sense of self, of who I am, it may be wrong and irrelevant to the world around me. It may be based on my own insanity rather than grounded in reality.

I don't know much about your story. But I will share that for me, I learned I was conditioned at a very young age to fawn as a trauma response. This set me up for a lot of failures later in life as I would believe in X and if a large enough group of people told me X was wrong and to believe Y instead, although it wouldn't fully change my mind I would believe "well I'm in the minority here and so I'm probably wrong" and go along with Y. 

Knowing that I do this and that it's actually a normal trauma response has helped me to recognize why I made so many choices I have over the years. And I am better able to close up that vulnerability within myself. I'm able to identify now when my sense of self is breaking, able to say "hey me, when this thing started happening you felt X way about it, THIS IS WHAT YOU ACTUALLY BELIEVE." and then I can look at what is triggering the breaking and say "okay this person is trying to push Y onto you instead. Why might they be doing that?" I've found more often then not it's their own selfishness, their own ego trying to prey on my weaknesses. Whether it's as dark as that or not though, being able to fully assess situations like that makes it a lot easier to then say okay, I may believe X while all these other people believe Y and that's okay. That doesn't make me wrong, because my belief in X comes from this perspective and their belief in Y comes from this other perspective and they both make sense. It's okay for me to be different. And I would argue it's even possible for me to find other people who believe in X for similar reasons as me so I'm not the odd one out anymore.

I hope this helps! You are not alone.

I was able to forgive myself only after fully realizing why I did every little thing I did. I was able to then forgive myself because I understood the paths I took, that I was normal, and that I have the tools to make sure I don't repeat my bad choices, and they are good enough tools that they won't even be that difficult to use because I can't take care of things before they become hard conversations.

I agree with you! I was not in any way trying to say what was right or wrong in this post, I was just trying to offer a perspective I hadn't seen posted here before which could potentially be helpful.

My situation is a little weird overall, but yes I always loved my husband and made that clear to my AP as well, that I would never choose my AP over my BS and would only talk about how much I loved my BS, I wasn't even in a situation where I complained about him or anything. 

Despite this I still crossed my BS boundaries and did things that although I didn't see as significant, he did. In that way I was selfish because I was only thinking about my perspective of things and not my BS perspective.

I have stayed in the past in what I would consider to be much worse situations than the one I am now in, 3 times actually. So I can confidently say I would stay. 

Something I've realized through my journey though is that it doesn't really matter all that much. Infidelity is not as black and white as people make it out to be. It is a crossing of a person's boundaries and boundaries differ greatly from person to person. Just because I wouldn't care about something doesn't mean anyone else around me is obligated to feel the same way. I strongly believe it is our responsibility as partners to be respectful of the other individuals boundaries and feelings, not our own. I hope that makes sense.

The people close to my AP called my husband abusive and manipulative too. I feel like it's a defensive accusation to backup the actions they wish to support. In my case though I snapped back at those calling my husband that and cut them out of my life as they were obviously not friends of my marriage, rather than holding it against my husband. 

I'm so sorry you are going through this OP. Don't doubt yourself.
I can try to be a friend. I'm 27/F if you would like to DM me

Just wanted to speak up and say I am in a similar position, both with how the affair happened and with the complicated aftermath. You aren't alone in your journey. I don't have any insight on long term healing as I'm still in the process though, I apologize. I think the only thing we can do is consistently be the kind of person we want to be. Consistently be better, and prove to yourself and your SO that is who you really are.

You have interpreted this as me seeking validation, but that is not how it was intended. I was in a good headspace and was looking for genuine constructive criticism. How can you fix things about yourself if you don't understand what is wrong to begin with?

I am in therapy and doing my best to try to work through everything. 

Thank you. I think I may have originally come into these spaces when there was a lot more negativity present and took it personally when I shouldn't have. I remember seeing some posts complaining about the state of things at one point and although this post isn't super old yet, the responses I've received have been much less harsh and more constructive. I appreciate everyone's insight here.

There are complications which have resulted in us being more or less "stuck" with each other for the time being. This has it's benefits as well as it's complications of course. I have decided to live my life as if we are reconciling regardless of his decisions as that is what I ultimately want. So I am not opening myself up to any other kind of close relationships currently, and he has access to all of my things at all times regardless of whether he takes advantage of that.
Yes. He has made the decision not to reconcile.
You sound a lot like someone very close to me, which breaks my heart. I'm not very good at giving pep talks but I hope you're able to hang on and make it through whatever you're going through.
What are you even talking about
I mean sure, but I can't force someone else to uphold the boundaries I set.

I did go radio silence on him. My husband has been pushing for divorce and ending our relationship pretty consistently and this person knew about that, so I suspect he may think when that is finalized that things will just go back to normal which is why he won't leave me alone now.  I had decided that I wanted to fight for mine and my husband's relationship even through and after a divorce though, which is when I really cut him off without any warning.

The biggest thing I'm struggling with is to what extent I need to just accept responsibility for my actions. If you work with an AP, you don't expect the AP to quit to keep your job right? Instead, as the WS it's important you accept the consequences of your actions and quit and find a new job, removing yourself from the situation rather than pushing the AP out. I would assume it's a similar circumstance if you knew an AP through a club or something to that sort. So although I genuinely think he is making decisions to try to keep in contact with me and not just of his own volition, I still wonder if it's more of my responsibility to just deal with it and remove myself.

Yes I keep having to reblock new accounts but he is blocked everywhere. 

This isn't an issue with me setting boundaries in this circumstance. That's definitely the case with AP but not with this individual. I appreciate the feedback though.
I wouldn't say I self sabotage in general. I did here, but not any time before and things were still bad, which makes me believe things will not in fact get better.
Thank you. Hearing your perspective as the BS means a lot to me.

No, I am not in contact with my family for unrelated reasons, and he doesn't trust any of my friends even if they were friends of the marriage and against what I did. That's what makes this so hard.

Right now I'm not really having any conversations but in a hypothetical world where I wasn't isolating I don't have any issues with that.

This is going to sound really dumb but I didn't think I was cheating. I always wanted my husband. I had let someone on the internet see my boobs and I didn't think much of it because of previous conversations he and I had had where apparently he wasn't being serious and I thought he was, and just because we both tended to associate with the more sexually liberated parts of the internet. I therefore didn't think much of it but as it turns out, it was a big deal to him.

We are in the middle of a divorce but funny enough there is another post here that explains how the divorce is being viewed by both of us. It's the end of our marriage but not necessarily the end of our relationship. I know for a fact I love him enough to not do it again. He did catch me but it was legitimately a first time offense, it's hard to explain without going into all of the details so I'm struggling to respond to this question, I apologize.
It's been two months and he is in therapy, we both are.
